evidence.observedFact: The business says a non-refundable $30 deposit is required to secure appointments and explicitly says this is intended to help manage its schedule and minimize last-minute cancellations; bookings without payment are canceled.

The business publicly advertises a 2026 repeat-visit promotion in which four visits earn the fifth service free and says it stamps customers' receipt records on each visit; it also advertises a different 2027 repeat-visit promotion.
The business asks customers to provide contact and birth-date information and states that it sends promotions, deals and incentives every week and around birthdays.

gaps.recommendedFix: Demonstrate an automated booking recovery workflow that complements the existing deposit policy and helps recover incomplete or disrupted bookings.
Digitize the existing manual stamped-receipt repeat-visit promotion into a trackable Places Rewards digital loyalty program.
Centralize permission-based promotion and birthday follow-up into an automated customer engagement workflow.

recommendedEntryOffer: Digital Loyalty + Booking Recovery Revenue Engine
notes: Observed facts come from the business-owned website. The loyalty gap refers specifically to an opportunity to digitize the publicly described manual stamped-receipt workflow; it does not claim the existing program is ineffective or quantify lost revenue.
